title: Chapter 256: Chairperson's Voice
html:
Lychee licked her lips in anticipation, as though recalling something delightful. She hurried into the restroom and had just taken a lipstick from her purse to touch up her makeup when her phone rang.

“An unknown number?” Lychee tossed the makeup kit back into her purse, irritated that the interruption had spoiled her mood. She composed herself until her voice sounded perfectly normal. “What a killjoy.”

Answering the phone, Lychee walked toward the studio door. “Hello. How can I help you?”

Her voice was like sparkling fruit wine—sweet, fresh, and intoxicating in large doses.

“No. 5 is dead. Come to the twenty-fourth floor of Fang Hwa Apartments immediately.” Unmoved by her charming voice, the caller went straight to the point.

“Dead?!” Lychee’s bleeding fingers slowly clenched, dripping blood onto the phone’s pink casing.

“I don’t care what No. 5 told you or what your relationship was. Come here now.”

“Now?” Lychee hesitated. Holding the phone in one hand, she cracked the door open with the other. The corridor beyond was utterly silent. “What does his death have to do with me? Why should I go to the twenty-fourth floor?”

“If you don’t want to die, come immediately!” The voice carried through the narrow gap in the door.

“Fine.” Lychee opened the door fully. She had taken barely half a step when a monstrous hammerhead hurtled toward her. Before she could scream, the blow sent her crashing back into the studio.

The pain reached her several seconds later, and a shriek tore from the studio. Chen Ge picked up the fallen phone and held it to his ear.

“No. 12?” A chilling rasp came from the other end. The caller was disguising his voice, yet it still sounded strangely familiar. Chen Ge tried to keep listening, but the man sensed something was wrong and immediately hung up.

I only heard a few words, but that alone was a valuable clue.

Standing in the dark corridor with Lychee’s phone, Chen Ge smiled. The society’s members were not supposed to know one another’s identities, but her caller was clearly an exception. He even knew of her connection to No. 5 and had called to warn her to flee.

That voice probably belongs to the chairperson controlling everything from the shadows.

Chen Ge compared it with the voices he had heard at the Ghost Stories Society. It definitely belonged to neither the first man on the left, No. 5, nor No. 10.

The possibilities are narrowing. Capture him, and the entire society will collapse.

After placing Lychee’s phone on the table, Chen Ge guarded the door and called Captain Yan. His team mobilized faster than the Western Jiujiang police and arrived in under ten minutes. Chen Ge put away the hammer, suggested searching Lychee’s home, and explained how she had murdered her ex-husband.

Everyone involved was taken away for questioning. At the station, Chen Ge met Captain Yan again. The slightly rotund police officer looked thoroughly exhausted.

“Captain Yan, long time no see.”

“Why does it feel as though I see you every day?” The sight of Chen Ge reminded Captain Yan of everything Inspector Lee had told him in private, and a headache began to form. Yet he could hardly blame the young man. He had awarded Chen Ge the medal and encouraged him to help. He had made his bed; now he had to lie in it.

“Well done, Xiao Chen!” Captain Yan’s smile looked strained. “But you acted far too recklessly.”

“I understand, but I couldn’t stand by while they were hurting innocent people.” Chen Ge did not deny acting rashly, but neither would he admit to anything he had not done. “Captain Yan, I had nothing to do with the kidnapper losing consciousness in the woods. I deliberately avoided his vital areas, and when he inexplicably passed out, I was the one who dragged him back.”

Captain Yan nodded. “I heard both drivers’ accounts. If you hadn’t arrived in time, things would have ended much worse.”

Captain Yan could tell that the drivers’ gratitude toward Chen Ge was sincere.

“So, may I leave now?” The Haunted House had a major promotion scheduled for the next day, and Chen Ge had to be there.

“Not yet. We still have plenty of questions. You need to finish your statement before you can go. Those are the rules.” Captain Yan and two other officers questioned Chen Ge about the cases, but he had prepared his answers in advance and handled them easily.

He described everything he could in detail and carefully omitted anything he could not explain. He also gave Captain Yan another important lead: the surveillance cameras at Hai Ming Apartments might have captured No. 5’s accomplices.

At 3:30 a.m., Captain Yan saw how exhausted Chen Ge was and allowed him to return to New Century Park. The moment he stepped into the Haunted House, however, he seemed to come back to life. Since eating Zhang Ya’s candy, Chen Ge had discovered that he needed little sleep to remain energetic—a secret he intended to keep to himself.

I should keep a low profile for a while. I may be able to endure this pace, but Captain Yan and his team might not.

In the staff break room, Chen Ge moved the white cat from his bed, lay down fully dressed, and fell asleep. At eight that morning, a phone call woke him. To his surprise, it was Gu Feiyu.

After visiting the Haunted House with the previous day’s group, Gu Feiyu had refused Chen Ge’s job offer. Money mattered, but his life mattered more. Chen Ge’s persuasion had worn him down, however, and he had agreed to give the work another try.

Murder by Midnight needs another actor. Xiao Gu will be perfect.

After washing his face and changing clothes, Chen Ge hurried to the park entrance to meet Xiao Gu.

“Brother Chen, I don’t think I have the talent to scare people. I thought about it all night. I appreciate the job offer, but I can’t let myself damage your Haunted House’s reputation.” Xiao Gu was an honest young man.

“That’s all right. I can teach you.” Chen Ge looked him over. “Come with me. We’ll get you into costume first.”

He led Xiao Gu into the dressing room. The sight of the blood-soaked doctor’s coat and a skin mask stitched from different faces immediately made the young man want to leave.

“Hold this—and take the hammer. Now give it a few swings for me.”
